Assert how many rows of each role a group has

Source: R/groups.R
ensure_counts.Rd

A checkpoint for the composition of groups: a family has exactly one reference person and at most two adults, a child has at most two parents, a person dies at most once. The groups that break a limit are reported, with every row of the group and a broken column naming the limits broken, such as "reference: 0 (needs 1)". Returns data, so it can sit in the middle of a pipeline.

Usage

ensure_counts(
  data,
  group,
  role = NULL,
  limits,
  success_msg = NULL,
  warn_msg = NULL,
  abort_msg = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or tibble, or a database or Arrow table: see Database and Arrow tables in checkpoints.

group

Column(s) identifying the group (tidy-select), e.g. c(family, year).

role

The role column (one column), or NULL to count rows.

limits

A named list of limits per role, or without role a single limit: a number, or the least and the most as two numbers.

success_msg

Message shown when the rule holds. If NULL (default), it is "Check passed: <message>" when warn_msg or abort_msg is given, so the console names every check that ran, and a description of the check otherwise.

warn_msg

Message shown when a group breaks a limit and no abort_msg is set. Defaults to a description of the check.

abort_msg

If provided, cli::cli_abort() is called with this message when the rule is broken. If NULL (default), a warning is issued instead.

Value

data invisibly, unchanged.

Details

Give the limits per role as a list, list(reference = 1, adult = c(1, 2)): one number for an exact count, two for the least and the most, with Inf for no upper limit. A group with no row of a role has 0 of it, so a family without a reference person breaks reference = 1. Roles not named are not limited. Without role, limits is one such number or pair, for the number of rows per group.

The same check covers relations and events: rows per child in a table of parents (limits = c(0, 2)), and deaths per person in a table of events (role = event, limits = list(death = c(0, 1))). To check a composition per family type, such as single parents with one adult, run it on the families of that type.

See also

describe_groups() to see the compositions first, ensure_references(), checkpoints.

Examples

families <- data.frame(
  family = c(1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4),
  role   = c("reference", "partner", "child", "reference", "child",
             "child", "reference", "reference")
)
ensure_counts(families, family, role,
              limits = list(reference = 1, partner = c(0, 1)))
#> Warning: Outside the limits: role per family
#> ℹ 3 rows
#>   In 2 groups
#>   reference: 0 (needs 1) in 1 group
#>   reference: 2 (needs 1) in 1 group
#> ℹ The rows:
#>     family role      broken
#>      <dbl> <chr>     <chr>
#>   1      3 child     reference: 0 (needs 1)
#>   2      4 reference reference: 2 (needs 1)
#>   3      4 reference reference: 2 (needs 1)

# At most two parents per child
parents <- data.frame(child = c("a", "a", "b", "b", "b"),
                      parent = c("m", "f", "m", "f", "x"))
ensure_counts(parents, child, limits = c(0, 2))
#> Warning: Outside the limits: rows per child
#> ℹ 3 rows
#>   In 1 group
#>   rows: 3 (needs at most 2) in 1 group
#> ℹ The rows:
#>     child broken                    parent
#>     <chr> <chr>                     <chr>
#>   1 b     rows: 3 (needs at most 2) m
#>   2 b     rows: 3 (needs at most 2) f
#>   3 b     rows: 3 (needs at most 2) x
